title: Fix 0.7.0 release-blocking review findings
description: Fix verified release blockers from the v0.7.0 review: interceptors must run exactly once on EmailClient/global delivery paths; Amazon SES raw sends must include explicit destinations for To/Cc/Bcc so Bcc recipients are delivered; SES MIME generation must retain inline attachments even without an HTML body; and the 0.7.0 changelog must explicitly document that MailError no longer implements Clone.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover interceptor single-application through EmailClient, SES SendRawEmail destination params include Bcc recipients, SES text-only inline attachments are emitted, changelog explicitly states MailError no longer implements Clone, and release gates pass.
close_reason: Fixed verified 0.7.0 release blockers: interceptors now apply exactly once across EmailClient, direct prepared, batch prepared, and cross-stack prepared paths; SES SendRawEmail includes explicit To/Cc/Bcc destinations and preserves inline attachments for text-only and empty-body messages; changelog documents that MailError no longer implements Clone; release gates passed.

title: Propagate attachment read and encoding errors
description:
Attachment::base64_data currently turns get_data failures into empty data via unwrap_or_default. This can deliver corrupted emails with empty attachments while returning Ok. Make attachment serialization fallible and propagate MailError through every provider path.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an Attachment with from_path_lazy pointing at a file.
2. Delete the file or make it unreadable before delivery.
3. Send through a provider that serializes attachments with base64_data.
4. Observe that the attachment content becomes empty instead of returning an error to the caller.
acceptance_criteria: Missing or unreadable lazy attachments cause delivery to fail; provider code propagates the original MailError; regression tests cover missing file and permission/read failure behavior.
close_reason: Fixed by making attachment base64 encoding fallible, propagating attachment read errors through provider builders, and adding regression tests for missing/unreadable lazy attachments.

title: Redact provider error bodies and harden MailError variant extensibility
description:
Several provider errors embed verbatim HTTP response bodies in MailError Display, which can include rejected recipients or other PII and then be logged by client error paths. MailError is #[non_exhaustive] at the enum level, but high-churn struct variants can still be constructed directly downstream, so adding fields for structured/redacted context remains breaking.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a provider error response whose body includes a recipient address or submitted payload detail.
2. Observe that MailError Display includes the raw body and client debug/error logging can emit it.
3. Try constructing MailError::ProviderError { .. } downstream and note that adding fields later would be breaking despite enum-level non_exhaustive.
acceptance_criteria: Provider error display paths avoid raw response-body PII by default; structured error context keeps bounded/redacted details where useful; high-churn MailError variants are made non_exhaustive or otherwise protected before adding fields; tests cover redaction behavior.

title: Tighten address and default-from validation consistency
description:
Address::to_ascii accepts malformed addresses such as user@ and @example.com, allowing JSON providers to send invalid addresses that lettre providers reject. Separately, EmailClient::from_env filters empty EMAIL_FROM but the global default_from helper uses raw env::var().ok(), so EMAIL_FROM="" diverges between paths.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Call Address::parse("user@").unwrap().to_ascii() or parse("@example.com").unwrap().to_ascii().
2. Observe invalid addresses are accepted for JSON providers.
3. Set EMAIL_FROM to an empty string.
4. Compare EmailClient::from_env and global deliver/default_from behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Address ASCII normalization rejects empty local/domain parts consistently; global default sender handling filters empty env vars the same way typed config does; tests cover malformed addresses and empty EMAIL_FROM.

title: Harden SMTP env configuration validation
description:
SMTP env config has three release-footgun paths: SMTP_PORT=465 defaults to StartTls even though 465 is implicit TLS; SMTP_USERNAME without SMTP_PASSWORD authenticates with an empty password; and SMTP_TLS=required is currently identical to starttls despite implying fail-closed semantics.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set SMTP_PORT=465 and omit SMTP_TLS.
2. Build SmtpConfig from env and observe it chooses StartTls instead of implicit TLS or a config error.
3. Set SMTP_USERNAME without SMTP_PASSWORD and observe config builds credentials with an empty password.
4. Set SMTP_TLS=required and observe it aliases starttls without extra enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: SMTP env config reconciles port 465 with TLS mode; username without password returns a clear configuration error; required TLS is either enforced distinctly or renamed/documented honestly; tests cover all cases.

title: Cache JMAP identity and drafts mailbox IDs
description:
JMAP session caching stores api_url/account_id but not the identity_id or drafts mailbox_id even though the session cache comment says identity ID is cached. Every send re-fetches both IDs, adding two extra round trips per delivery.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Send multiple emails through JMAP with the same JmapMailer.
2. Observe session discovery is cached but identity and drafts mailbox lookups still run for every delivery.
3. Note elevated latency and request volume versus a cache that keeps these stable IDs.
acceptance_criteria: JMAP caches identity_id and drafts mailbox_id for a discovered session/account where valid; repeated sends avoid redundant identity/mailbox requests; docs/comments match behavior; tests cover cache reuse.

title: Fix attachment and mechanical release quick wins
description:
Fix the surgical review findings that are low-risk for 0.7: zero-byte byte attachments are rejected as missing content; SMTP/Gmail fall back to text/plain when lettre rejects an attachment content type; provider error fallbacks eagerly allocate; SendGrid/Mailjet clone error messages before joining; config has redundant empty filters after optional_var; and from_env_with_ref allocates provider names unnecessarily.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create Attachment::from_bytes("empty.txt", Vec::new()).
2. Call get_data/base64_data or send it through a provider.
3. Observe AttachmentMissingContent even though an intentionally empty byte attachment is valid.
4. Build an SMTP/Gmail attachment with a content type lettre cannot parse.
5. Observe that it is silently labeled text/plain instead of octet-stream or an explicit error.
acceptance_criteria: Zero-byte byte attachments return empty data and encode to an empty base64 string; SMTP and Gmail invalid attachment content types no longer become text/plain; mechanical allocation cleanups are applied; regression tests cover zero-byte attachments and invalid MIME fallback; release gates pass.
close_reason: Fixed zero-byte byte attachments, changed SMTP/Gmail invalid attachment content-type fallback to application/octet-stream, applied mechanical allocation/config cleanups, added regression tests, and verified release gates.

title: Run 0.7.0 release hardening audit
description: Perform the missing full-repo release-hardening pass before 0.7.0: request a whole-codebase review, audit the crate against rust-skills categories, fix concrete release-relevant findings, and file follow-up Beads issues for larger or speculative improvements. Scope is production library quality, idiomatic Rust, lean dependencies, memory/performance sanity, documentation and release readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Full-repo code review has been requested and addressed; rust-skills audit findings are either fixed or filed; release quality gates pass locally and in CI; changelog/docs reflect release-relevant fixes; work is committed and pushed.
close_reason: Completed full-repo release hardening audit with independent code review and rust-skills pass. Fixed release blockers for all-features preview builds, SMTP TLS downgrade behavior, SES header safety, PII warning logs, CI feature coverage, packaging exclusions, poisoning-safe local/JMAP locks, and docs/changelog. Filed follow-up issues missive-v7j, missive-c6t, and missive-17b for non-blocking audit leftovers. Verified fmt, clippy, tests, feature matrices, WASM checks, package assembly, Beads lint, and dependency cycles.

title: Address WASM code review findings
description: The focused code review for wasm32 support found two Important issues: native-only SMTP feature gates emit secondary unresolved lettre errors on wasm, and supported WASM HTTP providers still pull Tokio unnecessarily. Fix both narrowly while preserving the lean target-specific design and verify native plus wasm checks.
acceptance_criteria: wasm,smtp fails with only the intended native-only feature diagnostic; wasm,resend no longer includes tokio in cargo tree; native full checks/tests and supported wasm checks/clippy pass.
close_reason: Addressed review findings by hiding lettre-backed error variants on wasm native-only feature combinations, removing the supported WASM Tokio dependency, documenting the fetch-compatible host requirement, and adding CI checks for the native-only diagnostic plus Tokio-free WASM provider tree. Verified native and wasm checks, clippy, tests, formatting, diff hygiene, and Beads health.

title: Add wasm feature flag ergonomics
description: GitHub issue #2 explicitly recommends a user-facing wasm feature so users can write missive = { features = ["wasm", "resend"] }. The underlying wasm support is implemented; add a clean marker feature, documentation, and CI coverage for that public Cargo feature shape.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo declares a wasm feature, docs show features = ["wasm", "resend"], CI verifies wasm provider checks with the feature included, and native/wasm verification still passes.
close_reason: Added public wasm marker feature, updated README/decision/changelog and CI to verify features = ["wasm", provider] on wasm32-unknown-unknown. Verified native and wasm checks.

title: Credit Mailjet issue and PR in release notes
description: Add explicit changelog attribution/linkage for the Mailjet provider detection fix from GitHub issue #3 and PR #4, and close the obsolete conflicting PR with a comment that credits the contributor and points to the landed main commit.
acceptance_criteria: CHANGELOG 0.7.0 links the Mailjet fix to issue #3 and PR #4 with contributor credit. PR #4 has a clear closing comment pointing to the landed commit. Changes are committed and pushed.
close_reason: CHANGELOG now credits and links GitHub issue #3 and PR #4 for the Mailjet provider detection fix, and PR #4 was closed with a superseding-main-commit comment crediting @emmiegit.

title: Handle pre-0.7 GitHub release blockers
description: Evaluate the pre-release GitHub items for 0.7.0: remove deprecated MailerExt::validate() from issue #1, port Mailjet EMAIL_PROVIDER support from issue #3 / PR #4 into the current config API, and record the WASM issue #2 release decision. Rust 1.96 features should be considered against the crate MSRV before adoption.
acceptance_criteria: MailerExt::validate() is removed from the public API. Mailjet can be selected explicitly with EMAIL_PROVIDER=mailjet and auto-detected from MAILJET_API_KEY/MAILJET_SECRET_KEY when the mailjet feature is enabled. Docs and changelog mention the 0.7 behavior. WASM and Rust 1.96 are explicitly decided for this release.
close_reason: Removed MailerExt::validate(), wired Mailjet into typed env configuration and detection, added Swoosh-aligned Mailjet tracking options, documented the Rust 1.96/MSRV and WASM release decisions, and verified format, tests, clippy, and Beads health.

title: Prepare 0.7.0 release metadata
description: The v0.7 cleanup introduced breaking public API and behavior changes. Bump the crate and docs from 0.6.2 to 0.7.0 and promote the changelog migration notes into a dated 0.7.0 release section that clearly calls out breaking changes.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock report version 0.7.0; README/docs dependency snippets use 0.7.0; CHANGELOG has a 0.7.0 section with breaking changes and migration notes; verification passes.
close_reason: Bumped crate metadata and documentation to 0.7.0 and expanded CHANGELOG with explicit breaking changes and migration notes.

title: Fix CI clippy unnecessary_sort_by lint
description: GitHub Actions Clippy fails on stable Rust 1.95.0 with clippy::unnecessary_sort_by in src/providers/amazon_ses.rs. Update the header sorting expression to satisfy current stable clippy without changing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: cargo clippy --features full --all-targets -- -D warnings passes locally; CI clippy job is fixed by a pushed commit.
close_reason: Replaced Amazon SES header sort comparator with sort_by_key and verified clippy with Rust 1.95.0 plus full tests.

title: Preserve source error chains in MailError
description: MailError currently derives Clone and stringifies underlying errors such as reqwest, lettre, serde_json, and IO errors. Redesign errors to preserve source chains for downstream diagnostics, retry classification, and observability.
acceptance_criteria: MailError variants store source errors where useful; std::error::Error::source exposes causal chains; Clone is removed unless there is a clear replacement strategy; provider tests assert useful error classification.
close_reason: MailError now preserves source chains for serde_json, reqwest, askama, lettre, SMTP transport, lettre address, and attachment IO errors; Clone was removed; error kind/status helpers were added; regression tests cover source chains and provider classification.

title: Introduce validated email preparation model
description: Validation is currently split between deliver wrappers and provider adapters, and direct Mailer::deliver calls can behave differently. Define a clear validation/preparation boundary, such as EmailDraft to PreparedEmail, so provider implementations receive a consistently valid message.
acceptance_criteria: Provider adapters receive a prepared/validated email type or shared validation path; direct provider use cannot bypass required validation accidentally; tests cover global/client/direct-mailer send paths.
close_reason: Added PreparedEmail as the validated delivery boundary, routed Mailer direct/client/facade paths through provider-aware preparation, migrated adapters to deliver_prepared/deliver_many_prepared, preserved SendGrid custom personalization validation, and added regression tests for direct mailer and facade validation.

title: Encapsulate public Email, Address, and Attachment fields
description: Core data structs expose representation directly, making invalid states easy and future refactors semver-breaking. Move toward private fields, accessors, and constructors/builders that preserve flexibility without freezing internals.
acceptance_criteria: Core struct fields are private or intentionally minimized; public getters/builders cover common use; serde compatibility and migration impact are documented.
close_reason: Made Email, Address, and Attachment fields crate-private, added read-only accessor APIs, updated integration tests and doctests to use accessors, preserved serde derives/field names, and documented field-access migration notes for v0.7.

title: Replace stringly provider_options with typed provider option APIs
description: Email::provider_options uses HashMap<String, serde_json::Value> for provider-specific behavior, which makes typos and type errors runtime-only. Add typed option APIs for provider-specific capabilities and keep a clearly marked raw escape hatch only where necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Common provider features like Resend scheduled_at/idempotency/tags have typed APIs; invalid option types fail at compile time or validation; raw JSON option use is documented as advanced escape hatch.
close_reason: Added ResendEmailExt typed helpers for tags, scheduled_at, idempotency key, and template payloads; documented provider_option as an advanced raw escape hatch; exported typed Resend option API; and covered typed option serialization with provider tests.

title: Replace core env auto-detection with explicit typed configuration
description: Environment variable probing is currently embedded in core delivery flow. Refactor toward explicit configuration structs and a from_env helper so env behavior is opt-in and testable rather than hidden global behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Provider config types validate required fields; from_env is isolated and testable; primary send path does not read process env; auto-detection order is documented or removed.
close_reason: Added explicit typed MailerConfig/provider config structs, testable from_env_with helpers, EmailClient::from_env(), documented auto-detection order, and moved global compatibility setup onto the explicit config path. Primary EmailClient::new delivery remains env-free.

title: Introduce instance-based EmailClient as the primary API
description: Move the architectural center from global deliver() to an explicit EmailClient configured by the application. Consumers should construct a client from typed config or a concrete provider and pass it through app state/dependency injection.
acceptance_criteria: Docs and examples use EmailClient first; EmailClient can send single and batch emails; global deliver remains only as an optional convenience or compatibility facade.
close_reason: Added the generic EmailClient primary API with default sender preparation, single and batch delivery, telemetry/metrics parity, Arc/reference mailer adapters, tests, and docs/examples leading with EmailClient while preserving global helpers as compatibility facades.

title: Remove PII from default telemetry
description:
deliver and deliver_with include recipient addresses and subject lines in info-level tracing spans. Library defaults should not emit email addresses or subjects to normal logs because consumers may forward logs to third-party observability systems.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install an info-level tracing subscriber in a consumer application.
2. Call missive::deliver or missive::deliver_with with a real recipient and subject.
3. Observe recipient addresses and subject text attached to the info-level missive.deliver span.
acceptance_criteria: Info-level spans/logs include provider, status, counts, and timing only; subject/address logging requires debug/trace or explicit opt-in; tests or snapshot assertions cover span fields where practical.
close_reason: Default delivery telemetry no longer records recipient addresses, subjects, or message ids at INFO/ERROR. Spans and outcome events now expose provider, recipient/attachment counts, status, and duration, with regression coverage for deliver and deliver_with.

title: Audit provider attachment handling for lazy data support
description:
Provider adapters handle attachments inconsistently. SMTP uses attachment.data directly, which bypasses lazy file loading, while API providers call base64_data. Audit all providers so eager and lazy attachments behave consistently and fail consistently.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an Email with a lazy path-based attachment.
2. Send it through SMTP and at least one HTTP provider test double.
3. Compare payloads and failure behavior.
4. Observe that providers do not consistently load lazy data or propagate lazy-read failures.
acceptance_criteria: Every provider either supports lazy attachments correctly or returns UnsupportedFeature; tests cover SMTP and at least one HTTP provider with lazy attachments.
close_reason: Confirmed provider attachment paths load lazy data or propagate attachment errors; added SMTP lazy attachment unit coverage and Resend HTTP adapter lazy payload coverage.

title: Decide target public API shape for v0.7
description:
Choose the target architecture before large breaking edits. Evaluate an instance-oriented EmailClient API, typed provider configuration, whether globals remain behind an optional facade, and how provider dispatch should work for both static and dynamic use cases.

## Rationale
The remaining v0.7 cleanup tasks are coupled. Public field encapsulation, env handling, provider options, validation, and dynamic dispatch all depend on the desired public API shape. A decision record should prevent incompatible partial refactors.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep global deliver as the primary API and harden internals only.
- Make EmailClient with typed config the primary API and keep globals as optional compatibility sugar.
- Split static generic clients from boxed dynamic clients.
- Defer breaking changes and patch only correctness bugs.
design:
# Decision 0001: v0.7 Public API Shape

Status: accepted

Issue: `missive-wdl.1`

Date: 2026-05-28

## Context

The 0.6 API optimizes for quick setup:

```rust
let email = Email::new()
    .to("user@example.com")
    .subject("Welcome")
    .text_body("Hello");

missive::deliver(&email).await?;
```

That convenience comes from process-global mailer state, environment auto-detection
inside `deliver`, public data fields, `HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>`
extension points, and an object-safe `Mailer` trait implemented with
`async_trait`. Those choices made the initial library simple, but they also make
the crate harder to use as an idiomatic Rust dependency in larger applications.

The v0.7 refactor should make the explicit, typed, instance-owned path the
primary API while keeping a compatibility path for small applications and tests.

## Decision

### Primary API

The primary API for v0.7 is an instance-owned client:

```rust
let mailer = ResendMailer::new(ResendConfig::new(api_key)?);
let client = EmailClient::new(mailer)
    .with_default_from(Address::parse("noreply@example.com")?);

let email = Email::builder()
    .to("user@example.com")
    .subject("Welcome")
    .text_body("Hello")
    .build()?;

client.deliver(email).await?;
```

`EmailClient<M>` owns or shares the provider, default sender, interceptors,
telemetry policy, and other delivery configuration. Applications should pass the
client through normal dependency injection mechanisms such as Axum state,
Actix data, or an application-owned `Arc`.

Delivery should consume the email by value on the primary path:

```rust
impl<M: Mailer> EmailClient<M> {
    pub async fn deliver(&self, email: Email) -> Result<DeliveryResult, MailError>;
}
```

This makes clone costs explicit. A caller that needs to reuse a message can clone
it intentionally, while providers and interceptors can avoid deep cloning by
moving or sharing large attachment payloads internally.

### Email Construction And Validation

`Email`, `Address`, and `Attachment` fields should become private. Public
construction should happen through builders and accessor methods.

`Email` remains a draft message type that can be prepared by a client. A new
validated delivery model should separate provider input from user construction:

```rust
let prepared = client.prepare(email)?;
mailer.deliver(prepared).await?;
```

`PreparedEmail` is the provider-facing type. It includes defaults applied by the
client and guarantees required delivery invariants such as a sender and at least
one primary recipient. Providers should not need to repeat basic validation.

Address constructors should return `Result` when parsing or normalization can
fail. Builder methods that accept strings can either validate immediately or
defer errors into `build`, but invalid addresses should not silently enter a
prepared email.

### Provider Configuration

Provider constructors should accept typed configuration structs:

```rust
let config = ResendConfig {
    api_key,
    base_url: None,
    timeout: None,
};
let mailer = ResendMailer::new(config)?;
```

Environment loading should move out of the core delivery path and into explicit
helpers:

```rust
let config = ResendConfig::from_env()?;
let client = EmailClient::new(ResendMailer::new(config)?);
```

This keeps runtime configuration errors visible at startup and avoids hidden
global initialization during delivery.

### Provider-Specific Options

The stringly `provider_options` map should stop being the primary provider
extension mechanism. Provider crates/modules should expose typed option structs
and extension traits gated by their provider feature:

```rust
let email = Email::builder()
    .to("user@example.com")
    .subject("Welcome")
    .text_body("Hello")
    .resend_tag("category", "welcome")
    .resend_scheduled_at(send_at)
    .build()?;
```

Internally, provider-specific values can be stored in a private typed extension
bag keyed by concrete option type. Custom providers should be able to define
their own option type without depending on raw string keys. JSON maps may remain
as an escape hatch behind clearly named methods such as
`with_raw_provider_option`, but those methods should not be used in primary
examples.

Template data should likewise move toward typed input:

```rust
email.with_template_data(&welcome_context)?;
```

`serde_json::Value` can remain an internal representation for providers that
need JSON payloads, but callers should pass serializable Rust values where
possible.

### Provider Dispatch Strategy

Static dispatch is the default:

```rust
type ResendClient = EmailClient<ResendMailer>;
```

This path should avoid dynamic dispatch and avoid boxing futures when the
provider type is known at compile time.

Dynamic dispatch remains available, but it should be explicit:

```rust
let client: EmailClient<BoxMailer> = EmailClient::boxed(mailer);
```

The target shape is:

- A static provider trait for normal generic use.
- A boxed adapter type for runtime provider selection.
- Runtime provider selection only when the application asks for it.

The follow-up native-async-trait work should evaluate whether `Mailer` can move
to native async trait syntax or an explicit `impl Future + Send` return while
providing an object-safe boxed adapter for dynamic dispatch.

### Global Facade Policy

The process-global `deliver`, `deliver_with`, `configure`, and `reset` APIs are
compatibility sugar, not the primary v0.7 design.

They may remain behind a `global` or `compat-global` Cargo feature for one
transition cycle, but docs should lead with `EmailClient`. The global facade
should delegate to an internally owned `EmailClient` and should not introduce
behavior that the instance API cannot express.

Environment auto-detection should also move behind an explicit feature and
helper, such as `EmailClient::from_env()` or `GlobalMailer::init_from_env()`.
Calling `deliver` should not silently choose a provider unless the compatibility
feature documents that behavior.

### Migration Constraints

v0.7 is allowed to make breaking changes because the crate is still pre-1.0, but
the migration should be staged and mechanical:

- Keep existing builder-style method names where they remain valid.
- Add accessors before making fields private.
- Prefer deprecation warnings before removing global functions when feasible.
- Provide a migration guide with before and after examples for global delivery,
  provider configuration, provider options, attachments, and tests.
- Keep feature flags granular so users do not compile providers they do not use.
- Avoid adding a Tokio requirement to provider-neutral construction APIs.

## Consequences

This decision unblocks the v0.7 refactor sequence:

- `missive-wdl.5` should introduce `EmailClient` and make it the documented
  primary delivery path.
- `missive-wdl.6` should move environment detection into typed configuration
  helpers.
- `missive-wdl.7` should replace raw provider option maps with typed provider
  option APIs.
- `missive-wdl.8` and `missive-wdl.9` should encapsulate message fields and add
  the validated preparation model.
- `missive-wdl.14` should evaluate and implement the static plus boxed provider
  dispatch strategy.

The existing 0.6 architecture notes remain useful as a description of the
current implementation, but this decision is the target architecture for the
breaking v0.7 cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Decision records preferred primary API, global-facade policy, provider dispatch strategy, and migration constraints.
close_reason: Accepted the v0.7 target API decision: EmailClient is the primary instance-owned API, globals remain compatibility sugar, provider dispatch uses static clients plus explicit boxed adapters, provider config/options become typed, and migration constraints are documented in docs/decisions/0001-v0-7-public-api.md.

title: Refactor missive toward an idiomatic Rust library API
description: Track the v0.7-style cleanup needed to make missive feel like a high-quality Rust library rather than an app-style/global facade. This covers explicit client configuration, typed provider options, safer data models, attachment correctness, telemetry defaults, error sources, and migration documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Primary library API is instance-based; correctness bugs are fixed; breaking changes have migration guidance; remaining global helpers are clearly optional convenience APIs.
close_reason: All architectural cleanup child issues are complete, verified, committed, and pushed.

title: Design deterministic multi-value email headers
description: Email headers are stored as HashMap<String, String>, which gives nondeterministic provider iteration order and silently clobbers duplicate header names. Some valid email headers, such as References or List-Unsubscribe, may need repeated values or stable ordering. This is likely a breaking API change and should be designed deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: A design or implementation chooses Vec<(String, String)>, IndexMap, or another deterministic multi-value representation; migration impact is documented; providers preserve stable header order and duplicates where supported.

title: Add stacked EmailClient interceptor regression guard
description: The 0.7 release-blocker fix added counting regression coverage for single interceptors through EmailClient and prepared paths, but stacked interceptors through EmailClient are only covered by hand reasoning and by idempotent header tests. Add a non-idempotent stacked-interceptor test so future prepared/raw routing changes cannot reintroduce double application.
acceptance_criteria: A test sends through EmailClient with two stacked non-idempotent interceptors and asserts each interceptor applies exactly once in the expected order; focused interceptor tests and release gates pass.
close_reason: Added a non-idempotent stacked EmailClient interceptor regression test that asserts outer/inner interceptors each run once in order, documented the raw deliver invariant, and verified focused tests plus release gates.

title: Bring SendGrid preparation back through shared validation
description: SendGrid overrides prepare_email and currently bypasses shared validate_required_fields while also parsing provider_options personalizations separately from request building. Rework this so future shared validation rules apply to SendGrid and expensive personalization parsing is not duplicated.
acceptance_criteria: SendGrid preparation reuses shared validation or an equivalent central helper; personalizations are parsed once per delivery path; regression tests cover missing required fields and custom personalizations.

title: Normalize inline attachment content IDs across providers
description:
Inline attachment content_id handling diverges across providers: Resend only emits content_id when one is explicitly present, while Mailtrap forces content_id to the filename and ignores a user-supplied content_id. Align provider serialization so the same Email has consistent cid behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an inline attachment with content_id("hero") and reference cid:hero from an HTML body.
2. Serialize/deliver the same Email through Resend and Mailtrap adapter tests.
3. Observe that Resend and Mailtrap produce different content_id behavior, and Mailtrap can ignore the explicit content_id.
acceptance_criteria: Resend and Mailtrap preserve explicit content_id values; inline attachments without explicit content_id have documented consistent behavior; provider tests cover both cases.

title: Validate Mailjet provider option types
description:
Mailjet tracking options currently use as_bool/as_str and silently ignore provider_options values with the wrong JSON type, such as track_opens set to the string "true". Decide whether to reject malformed option types during preparation or introduce typed Mailjet options, then cover the behavior with tests.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build a Mailjet email with provider_option("track_opens", "true") or a non-string url_tags value.
2. Deliver through the Mailjet adapter test double.
3. Observe that the malformed option is omitted silently instead of returning an explicit error.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed Mailjet tracking/url tag option types produce an explicit MailError or typed API prevents invalid values; tests cover track_opens, track_clicks, and url_tags.

title: Update GitHub checkout action before 0.7.0
description: Release hardening follow-up: GitHub Actions reports Node 20 deprecation warnings for actions/checkout@v4. Update CI to actions/checkout@v6 and verify workflow syntax/diff before the 0.7.0 release.
close_reason: Updated CI to actions/checkout@v6, verified workflow YAML parsing, confirmed no whitespace errors, and checked all checkout references use v6.

title: Add cautious coding guidance to agent docs
description: Fold the reusable concepts from multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills CLAUDE.md into this repository's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md without disrupting the existing Beads workflow instructions.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md both include concise guidance for thinking before coding, simplicity, surgical changes, and verifiable goals. Existing Beads instructions remain intact. Changes are committed and pushed.
close_reason: Added cautious coding operating principles to AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, preserving the existing Beads workflow and local cargo guidance.

title: Plan WASM support feature track
description: Track GitHub issue #2 as a dedicated post-0.7 feature effort. WASM support needs target-specific work across global state, env loading, filesystem-backed attachments, reqwest features, getrandom/chrono time support, provider feature compatibility, and async trait Send bounds. Do not treat this as a 0.7.0 blocker unless the release scope changes.
design: WASM support should be target-driven, not a broad runtime abstraction. Use Rust's recommended cfg(all(target_family = "wasm", target_os = "unknown")) for wasm32-unknown-unknown. Keep native dependencies native: uuid enables js only for wasm, reqwest uses JSON-only wasm features and native TLS/multipart on native, tokio/fs remains native-only. Path-based attachments are unsupported on wasm with explicit MailError::UnsupportedFeature; byte attachments work everywhere. HTTP JSON providers compile on wasm; native TCP/server providers and Mailgun multipart get clear compile_error guards. Add CI wasm cargo check gates and docs describing supported providers and limitations. Rust 1.96 compatibility: avoid raw wasm imports/undefined symbols and rely on wasm-bindgen-backed crates.
acceptance_criteria: A WASM design is written, feature/target gates are selected, wasm32-compatible providers are identified, and CI includes at least a wasm32 compile check before implementation is considered complete.
close_reason: Implemented wasm32-unknown-unknown support with target-specific dependencies, wasm-safe attachment/config/global-state behavior, provider feature gates, CI wasm checks, and documentation. Verified native full checks/tests plus wasm cargo check and clippy.

title: Write migration guide for breaking v0.7 library API changes
description: The cleanup will likely require breaking API changes. Document migration from global deliver/env setup to EmailClient/config, typed provider options, private fields/builders, and updated attachment/error behavior.
acceptance_criteria: README and docs include old-to-new examples; breaking changes are listed with rationale; CHANGELOG has a migration section.
close_reason: Added v0.7 migration guide coverage, README old-to-new examples, CHANGELOG migration notes, and updated docs snippets for accessor APIs.

title: Audit address formatting and header support across providers
description: Some provider adapters use Address::formatted rather than RFC5322-safe formatting, and SMTP currently ignores custom headers. Audit provider-specific expectations for names, IDNs, reply-to behavior, and custom headers to prevent malformed messages or silently dropped fields.
acceptance_criteria: Provider address formatting is consistent and documented; tests cover display names with quotes/commas and IDN domains; unsupported custom headers fail or are documented instead of silently ignored.
close_reason: Standardized provider address serialization with RFC 5322 quoting for mailbox-string APIs and IDNA/Punycode domains across structured providers, added SMTP/Gmail custom header support with invalid-name errors, documented behavior, and added provider/header regression tests.

title: Evaluate native async trait API versus boxed Mailer adapter
description:
The current Mailer trait uses async_trait to support dyn Mailer. Decide whether the redesigned primary API should use native async fn in traits for static dispatch, a boxed object-safe adapter for runtime dispatch, or keep async_trait for pragmatic compatibility.

## Rationale
Native async functions in traits reduce boxing for static dispatch, but they are not object-safe. Missive currently relies on Arc<dyn Mailer> for runtime provider selection, so changing this affects the entire provider and client architecture.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep async_trait everywhere for object-safe simplicity.
- Use native async fn in the primary trait and provide a separate boxed adapter.
- Avoid a public async trait and make EmailClient own provider enums/config directly.
- Delay this choice until after EmailClient design is settled.
acceptance_criteria: Decision explains object-safety tradeoff, dispatch modes, migration cost, and recommended public trait/API shape.
close_reason: Recorded Decision 0002: keep async_trait as the v0.7 object-safe Mailer trait, make EmailClient<M> the primary API, keep Arc<dyn Mailer> as explicit runtime dispatch, and defer a native-async/static-plus-boxed split until benchmarks justify the migration.

title: Reduce Email cloning and attachment memory amplification
description: prepare_email, interceptors, local storage, and provider conversion paths clone Email values. Large Vec<u8> attachments can be copied repeatedly. Audit clone paths and shift large attachment data to bytes::Bytes, Arc<[u8]>, or consuming APIs where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Large attachment data is not duplicated by routine Email clones; benchmarks or targeted tests demonstrate lower clone cost; API ownership model is documented.
close_reason: Implemented shared immutable attachment byte storage with clone-sharing tests and documented ownership semantics.

title: Move lazy attachment file reads off async worker threads
description: Lazy attachment reads use std::fs::read in delivery paths. For async runtimes, large or slow file reads should use tokio::fs or spawn_blocking so send operations do not block executor worker threads.
acceptance_criteria: Lazy attachment file reads are async-runtime friendly; implementation works without forcing Tokio on non-Tokio users or clearly gates runtime-specific behavior; tests cover lazy file sends.
close_reason: Added feature-gated Tokio-backed lazy attachment reads for async providers, migrated provider serialization paths to await attachment I/O, documented the feature gate, and covered async/lazy sends with tests.

title: Remove global LocalMailer storage coupling
description: local_storage() uses a process-global OnceLock for preview integration. Refactor preview/local mailer setup so applications pass an explicit MemoryStorage instance to LocalMailer and the preview UI, enabling isolated concurrent sandboxes and tests.
acceptance_criteria: Preview examples use explicit storage wiring; multiple independent local mailboxes can coexist in one process; local_storage global is removed, deprecated, or isolated behind compatibility facade.
close_reason: Removed the process-global LocalMailer storage singleton, made env local mailers create ordinary isolated LocalMailer instances, left local_storage as a deprecated non-creating compatibility facade, updated preview docs to pass storage explicitly, and added isolation/regression tests.

title: Define duplicate-recipient delivery semantics
description:
Email::all_recipients() currently concatenates To, Cc, and Bcc without deduplicating. Amazon SES now sends explicit Destinations.member.N values for all recipients, so the same address listed in multiple recipient groups can appear more than once. Other providers also serialize recipient groups directly, so this needs a cross-provider semantics decision rather than an SES-only patch.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an Email with the same address in To and Cc or Bcc.
2. Deliver through Amazon SES.
3. Observe duplicate Destinations.member.N entries for the same mailbox, which may cause duplicate delivery or double quota usage depending on SES behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Missive documents or enforces duplicate-recipient semantics consistently; if deduping is chosen, SES explicit destinations and other provider serializers avoid duplicate mailbox delivery while preserving intended headers where applicable.

title: Consolidate provider wire serialization conventions
description: Provider address/header serialization is duplicated across adapters in two conventions, and the doubled Mailer prepared/unprepared surface makes wrapper behavior easy to drift. Evaluate a small central helper for provider address parts and a simpler prepared delivery pipeline without expanding public API surface unnecessarily.
acceptance_criteria: A design or implementation centralizes repeated address-to-wire conversion; Mailer wrapper forwarding has tests for prepared and unprepared paths; any trait/API changes are documented as breaking or deferred with rationale.

title: Remove blocking preview attachment reads from async handlers
description:
Preview attachment downloads still use blocking std::fs::read in async handlers for lazy/path attachments. Even though preview is dev-only, this should use the async attachment accessor or offload blocking disk reads.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Store a local preview email with a lazy/path attachment.
2. Download that attachment through the preview handler.
3. Observe that the handler reads the file with blocking filesystem I/O on the async request path.
acceptance_criteria: Preview attachment download path uses get_data_async or spawn_blocking-backed reads; tests still cover attachment downloads.

title: Reduce avoidable delivery-path allocations
description: Several hot paths have avoidable allocation or clone costs: IDNA conversion runs for already-ASCII domains, global deliver_many clones batches before EmailClient preparation, SES MIME assembly uses transient format allocations and char-by-char base64 wrapping, and SendGrid personalizations can be cloned/deserialized twice.
acceptance_criteria: ASCII address serialization has a cheap fast path; batch/global delivery avoids redundant full-email clones where practical; SES MIME base64/header assembly avoids obvious transient allocations; benchmarks or focused tests guard behavior.

title: Make JMAP builder reject missing auth
description: The 0.7.0 audit found that JmapBuilder::build can construct a mailer with an empty Basic auth header when neither credentials nor bearer_token is configured. This is not release-blocking because environment configuration always requires auth, but direct builder users should get a local configuration error instead of an opaque unauthenticated provider request.
acceptance_criteria: JMAP exposes a fallible builder path or makes build fallible; direct builder use without credentials or bearer token returns MailError::Configuration; tests cover missing basic and bearer auth cases; docs/examples show the fallible API.

title: Evaluate native reqwest feature slimming
description: The 0.7.0 release hardening audit noted that the shared native reqwest dependency enables multipart for every HTTP provider even though only Mailgun needs multipart forms. This is acceptable for 0.7.0, but a focused dependency-design pass may reduce compile time and transitive footprint without hurting feature ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo features are audited for reqwest feature ownership; multipart is enabled only when needed if Cargo target/feature constraints allow it cleanly; cargo tree output demonstrates any reduction; provider and WASM matrices continue to pass.

title: Preserve structured provider error response context
description: The 0.7.0 audit found several provider adapters collapse response-body read failures, JSON/XML parse failures, or provider error bodies into generic strings. This can make production debugging harder after HTTP failures. Treat this as a structured error design pass rather than a rushed release edit.
acceptance_criteria: Provider error handling preserves HTTP status, a bounded response body snippet, and parse/read source errors where available; tests cover malformed provider error responses for representative JSON and XML providers; MailError API changes are documented if needed.

title: Audit docs for stale versions and feature-bundle accuracy
description: Documentation has version drift and bundle descriptions that may not exactly match Cargo features. Audit README and docs so examples, versions, and feature bundle descriptions match Cargo.toml.
acceptance_criteria: README/docs versions match crate version policy; feature bundle descriptions match Cargo.toml; preview docs no longer reference stale versions.
close_reason: Fixed stale Missive dependency versions and aligned documented feature bundles with Cargo.toml.
